title: Implementing a Fabric Data Architecture — Thin Slice to Operations
purpose: Shows the minimum implementation chain from an owned source contract through Fabric workloads and OneLake to a governed, observable data product.
accessibleSummary: A three-stage implementation architecture. An owned source and service boundary scopes a thin delivery slice. Fabric workloads then ingest, transform, and serve that slice over shared OneLake data. Governance, operational evidence, recovery, and acceptance complete the path before the pattern is scaled.
longDescription: Implementation starts with ownership, source and output contracts, identity, and recovery expectations. A deliberately small vertical slice then uses the Fabric workload best suited to each responsibility while sharing data through OneLake. The slice is only accepted when permissions, lineage, quality, monitoring, replay, and support evidence are proven. The first and last stages are architecture patterns; the shared workload and OneLake behavior is grounded in Fabric product documentation.

nodes.label: Owned implementation boundary
nodes.summary: Name the owner, source contract, output contract, identity boundary, and recovery objective before provisioning the slice.
nodes.detail: This is the delivery boundary for one data product, not a generic platform programme. It fixes who owns failures, what data may enter, what consumers may rely on, and what evidence proves a successful run.
nodes.whyItMatters: Without a bounded contract, shared workspaces and reusable frameworks hide ownership and make failures difficult to reconcile.

processing: Define success, rollback, and recovery evidence
drill.example: A sales slice owns one CRM extract, one conformed customer table, one warehouse fact, and one certified report with a daily completion signal and named support owner.
failureModes: Framework-first delivery with no proven product
Secrets or environment settings embedded in code

nodes.label: Unified Fabric delivery slice
nodes.summary: Use role-oriented Fabric workloads for ingestion, transformation, serving, and BI while keeping the slice inside one shared environment.
nodes.detail: Fabric combines Data Factory, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence, Power BI, and other workloads in one SaaS environment. Pipelines can orchestrate movement, notebooks, Spark jobs, SQL, stored procedures, and dbt jobs, letting the slice use distinct engines without constructing a separate integration platform.
nodes.whyItMatters: A vertical slice proves the real hand-offs between engines, storage, identity, deployment, and operations before reusable abstractions multiply them.

evidence.note: Fabric workloads run in one environment and share data and items without teams manually integrating separate services.
Data Factory pipelines orchestrate movement, notebooks, Spark jobs, SQL, stored procedures, control flow, and dbt activities.

processing: Transform with the selected Spark or SQL engine
outputs: A consumer-facing table, model, report, or API
drill.example: A pipeline copies CRM changes, a Spark notebook conforms customer keys, Warehouse T-SQL builds the sales fact, and Power BI serves a certified model.
failureModes: Choosing engines by team habit instead of workload shape
A partial run publishes incomplete output

nodes.label: Governed OneLake outcome
nodes.summary: Complete the slice with shared Delta data, inherited governance, operational signals, and a tested recovery path.
nodes.detail: Fabric data items persist tabular data in OneLake using Delta Parquet, allowing multiple engines to work over the same physical data. Fabric centralizes permissions, sensitivity labels, auditing, and catalog behavior across the shared platform; architecture acceptance must add measured quality, monitoring, and recovery evidence around those controls.
nodes.whyItMatters: A technically successful query is not a production-ready data product until access, freshness, lineage, replay, and support behavior are observable and repeatable.

evidence.note: Fabric data items persist tabular data in OneLake as open Delta Parquet so multiple engines can use the same physical data.
Fabric provides centralized governance through the OneLake Catalog and built-in Purview controls.

processing: Capture lineage, quality, run, and capacity telemetry
Exercise rollback, replay, and support hand-off
outputs: A reusable pattern proven by one real slice
drill.example: The sales slice is accepted only after a failed daily load is replayed safely, the report remains on the last complete version, and support can identify the failed stage from run evidence.
controls: Alert, replay, rollback, and ownership runbook
failureModes: Monitoring exists but has no accountable responder

edges.label: publishes governed data and operational evidence

walkthrough.title: 1. Bound ownership and acceptance
walkthrough.explanation: Start with one owned contract and the evidence required to call it production-ready.

walkthrough.title: 2. Prove the full Fabric hand-off
walkthrough.explanation: Deliver a thin vertical slice through the workloads and engines it genuinely needs.

walkthrough.title: 3. Accept through operations
walkthrough.explanation: Verify shared storage, governance, observability, replay, rollback, and support before scaling the pattern.
